cohort: The study included 1971 participants (1062 females) from a UK prospective birth cohort, originally recruiting over 15,000 pregnant women in 1991-1992, with bone outcomes measured at age 17 years.
finding: Breech presentation at birth was associated with lower adolescent tibia bone mineral content, density, periosteal circumference, cross-sectional moment of inertia, and cross-sectional area, and lower hip cross-sectional area in females, suggesting a long-lasting influence of prenatal skeletal loading on development.
mod_finding: Adjustment for delivery method as a potential mediator did not substantially affect the associations between breech presentation and bone outcomes.
